sahneler.metin: A crew of smokejumpers parachuted onto a wildfire in Montana.
Within hours the fire raced up the slope, and thirteen men were fatally burned.
They were heading downhill toward the river.
They couldn't see the fire had jumped ahead of them.
Wind and dry grass drove it uphill faster than they could run.
Their foreman lit an escape fire and lay down in the ashes.
The others didn't follow. He survived.
The Forest Service redesigned its training.

aciklama:
Mann Gulch overran a crew of smokejumpers in Montana. The cause: a fire on a steep grassy slope outrunning men who couldn't see it had spotted ahead.
